page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.4xlarge is a high clock speed, compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a base clock speed of 3.3 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core, backed by 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Advanced vector instructions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 are present alongside AES cryptography acceleration.

The hardware configuration includes no bundled local storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps, requiring remote cloud storage volumes for all persistent data operations. In benchmark evaluations, the instance performs consistently within average thresholds across both single-core and multi-core processing. Stress-ng returned scores of 1562.49 in single-core and 16538.21 in multi-core tests, complemented by a Geekbench multi-core score of 8021.0. Large-block memory tests yielded 64.29 GB/s read and 38.96 GB/s write throughput, while Redis SET operations reached 15.27 million operations per second.

Resource allocation efficiency is geared toward compute intensity rather than capacity scaling. With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio and the absence of hardware accelerators such as GPUs, the server experiences throughput limitations on memory-heavy tasks; for instance, LLM prompt processing on a 7B parameter model falls into the lower 25th percentile at 23.28 tokens per second. Consequently, ecs.hfc7.4xlarge is most suitable for CPU-bound computational workloads, software compilation, batch encoding, in-memory caching clusters, and high-throughput static web serving.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc7.4xlarge is a compute-focused virtual machine instance featuring a 3.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8369HB processor with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores. The instance provides 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation suited for compute-heavy applications. Advanced CPU flags such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES are supported. The instance includes 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without integrated local storage, and contains no hardware accelerators. Benchmark results demonstrate consistent middle-tier performance across single-core and multi-core suites, highlighted by 15.27 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.68 GB/s static web serving throughput. Because memory capacity is bounded relative to vCPU count, memory-intensive jobs and large neural models face performance limits. The configuration is optimal for software compilation, data compression pipelines, caching tiers, and general CPU-intensive processing tasks.
